title.narrative: Emergency Shelter and NFI Assistance for Displaced and Returnee Families in Gaza

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe humanitarian situation in Gaza has reached catastrophic proportions due to the ongoing hostilities, mass displacement, and extensive destruction of shelter infrastructure. As of early 2025, 1.9 million people remain internally displaced, enduring severe overcrowding in collective shelters, makeshift settlements, and host communities. Numerous homes have been either severely damaged or entirely destroyed, leaving hundreds of thousands of families without adequate shelter solutions. The scarcity of essential household items, combined with extreme weather conditions and overcrowded living spaces, has further compounded health, safety, and protection risks for these vulnerable populations.ltbrgtIn response, NRC’s shelter intervention is closely aligned with OCHA’s 2025 Flash Appeal and the Shelter Cluster response strategy, with a primary focus on providing emergency shelter solutions, essential non-food items (NFIs), and winterization support. The project will prioritize North Gaza, Khan Younis, and Rafah, targeting displaced families residing in collective shelters, returnees to damaged homes, and host communities that are struggling to accommodate an influx of displaced populations.ltbrgtTo ensure efficient and effective implementation, NRC will collaborate with the Beit Lahia Development Association (BLDA), leveraging their local expertise and established presence. BLDA will support key activities such as assessments, targeting, storage, and distribution of shelter materials and NFIs. Furthermore, BLDA will play a critical role in coordinating with local authorities and engaging with communities to guarantee the timely delivery of assistance, thereby reinforcing the overall humanitarian response in the region.ltbrgtThe selection of intervention sites will follow a rigorous, evidence-based approach in coordination with the Shelter Cluster and in line with its guidance. Priority will be given to areas experiencing high displacement density, extensive shelter damage, and critical gaps in humanitarian assistance. Considerations such as accessibility, security conditions, and the presence of vulnerable groups—including female-headed households, persons with disabilities (PwD), and the elderly—will guide site selection. This targeted methodology ensures that the most vulnerable populations receive prompt and adequate shelter support. The project will also integrate the needs of returnees into the NRC and Shelter Cluster Ceasefire Plan, facilitating a safe and sustainable reintegration process for displaced families. NRC will assist returnees with emergency shelter support, minor repair materials, and technical guidance to promote self-recovery efforts, while also coordinating with local authorities and partners to ensure that returns are voluntary, dignified, and in line with broader ceasefire stabilization objectives.ltbrgtThe project’s key activities will include:ltbrgt The distribution of Sealing-Off Kits and Framing Kits to repair and reinforce temporary and partially damaged shelters.ltbrgt The provision of essential NFIs, such as bedding sets, kitchen sets, washing sets, and thermal sleeping items.ltbrgt The prepositioning of shelter materials to enhance response capacity and alleviate logistical challenges.ltbrgt Close coordination with the Shelter Cluster, OCHA, and other implementing partners to ensure the efficient and timely distribution of aid.ltbrgtThrough these activities, NRC aims to enhance the safety, dignity, and resilience of conflict and displacement-affected populations. A total of 11,200 individuals (2,000 households) will directly benefit from this intervention, including the most vulnerable groups including those living in makeshift shelters or damaged homes. The project will provide protection from harsh weather conditions, improve living conditions, and restore shelter solutions, ensuring a dignified and secure environment for displaced families.ltbrgtlt/pgt
